scope: Bounded primary-source and equivalent-term audit; no exhaustive novelty or conjugacy claim.

sources.title: A note on overrelaxation in the Sinkhorn algorithm
sources.examined: Equations (2) and (7), local block-SOR derivation in section 2, global sufficient interval in Theorem 3.
sources.consequence: The common-rate algorithm and its two-projective-space formulation are prior art. The local fixed-point spectral relation is already connected to SOR.

sources.title: Overrelaxed Sinkhorn-Knopp Algorithm for Regularized Optimal Transport
sources.examined: Section 4.1 on fixed-rate nonconvergence; section 4.3, Theorem 1 and equations (26)-(30).
sources.consequence: Nonconvergence is known. Distinct adaptive relaxation functions for the two projections are also known; their Lyapunov safeguard differs from the fixed above-2 rates tested here.

sources.title: On the modified successive overrelaxation method
sources.examined: Publisher-indexed introduction and displayed block formulation; direct open returned HTTP 403, but the primary publisher text was available in search retrieval.
sources.consequence: Two fixed relaxation rates assigned to red and black equation blocks are established MSOR practice, attributed there to Young. No priority is claimed for the block-rate design.

sources.title: Chaotic Polynomial Automorphisms: Counterexamples to Several Conjectures
sources.authors: Arno van den Essen and Engelbert Hubbers
sources.examined: Author-hosted published paper, introduction and Theorem 1.1 with proof.
sources.consequence: Stable pointwise Jacobian spectra do not in general imply global convergence. The explicit examples used here as prior art have escaping orbits; they do not classify the sampled matrix-scaling sets.

unresolved: No matching classification of the selected matrix-scaling configurations was identified in the examined sources.
The selected maps are smooth diffeomorphisms. No intrinsic obstruction to equivalence with known invertible chaotic maps has been established.
No trapping certificate or infinite-time Lyapunov theorem identifies either portrait as a chaotic attractor.
No numerical probability is assigned to historical novelty.
